narrative:
The model estimates a 59% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while the rest had six or more years. This limited tenure signals higher turnover risk to the system.

The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most important driver and pushed the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model predicted would stay had not received outside opportunities.

Your length of time with this current organization (also 1-5 years) was the third strongest influence and further increased the likelihood of departure. Like overall experience, this is shorter than what the model typically sees in employees expected to remain.

Taken together, these three aspects of your career stage and external options outweighed other details such as your satisfaction levels or work conditions. The organization should discuss retention measures with you, while you may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals.
